newsitem.title: USA: House sets up panel to review ethics process.
newsitem.headline: House sets up panel to review ethics process.

text.p: House leaders Wednesday named a 12-member bipartisan task force to review the ethics process, which was badly strained during the investigation and punishment of Speaker Newt Gingrich.

Republican Leader Dick Armey of Texas and Democratic Leader Richard Gephardt of Missouri also said there would be a two month moratorium on filing new charges with the Ethics Committee while the task force completed its work.

"After the past few tumultuous months, I think we must have a brief cooling-off period where members can sit back and examine where the ethics process works, where it doesn't and how it might be improved -- and in a climate temporarily free from potential ethics charges," Armey said in a House speech.

He was refering to the investigation started nearly two years ago of Gingrich over charges that he misused tax free foundations to help finance a partisan government college course he thought and then gave misleading information to the committee about it.

Democrats and Republicans clashed for several months over Democratic charges that majority Republicans were delaying punishing Gingrich until he was re-elected Speaker Jan. 7. Two weeks later, the committee and then the full House voted to reprimand Gingrich and fine him $300,000 for the violations, marking the first time a speaker had been rebuked.
Critics have charged that it is hard for members of Congress to discipline their colleagues, especially someone in a leadership position.

Armey and Gephardt each named six members of the task force with Republican Bob Livingston of Louisiana and Democrat Ben Cardin of Maryland as co-chairs. They were asked to report to the leaders on how the ethics process might be improved.
